text:
maya: Quick question — we hit a canary race yesterday where runtime had an old penalty for a route and served degraded capacity for ~90s. Do we prefer runtime-local penalties with TTLs or authoritative policy lookups on each decision?

dominic: Ugh. Can you drop the logs here? link: https://internal.redwood/logs/4321 (redacted)

maya: Paste of the relevant lines:
``` 
2026-03-18T14:12:03Z router=rt-12 route=tenant-A penalty_seq=47 applied_penalty=0.4
2026-03-18T14:12:03Z policy-update service responded seq=49
2026-03-18T14:13:33Z router=rt-12 route=tenant-A penalty_seq=47 still in cache
```

olivia: TL;DR — we need something hybrid. Runtime-only gives lowest latency but you get stale state issues. Service-only gives correctness but adds RTT and outage blast radius. Hybrid: local cache with seq/tombstone + short TTL + async delta stream.

ryan: +1 to hybrid. Practical sketch: policy service is authoritative (seq numbers). Runtime keeps (seq, penalty, applied_at). On decision: if local.seq == latest_known_seq -> use local. If not known and route is latency-sensitive -> issue immediate read to policy service; else use local and schedule refresh. Also expose `max_staleness_ms` per route.

dominic: How do we get "latest_known_seq" cheaply across regions? We can't RPC every decision.

olivia: Use a low-cost delta stream (pubsub) and local snapshot on startup. Delta message: `route_id|seq|patch` — apply in-order. For misses, runtime can fetch a snapshot from regional cache. Add an eviction TTL so we don't accumulate ancient routes.

maya: Sounds good. What about invalidation storms on deploys? If policy changes a lot, every router might fetch snapshots.

ryan: Avoid thundering herd with jittered backoff + staggered snapshot windows. Also use a small bloom filter broadcast of changed route ids so only impacted routers fetch.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: notice: policy-service v2 will be deployed to canary group tomorrow at 09:00 PT :rocket:

maya: For testing: can we add a sim in the routing-sim harness that replays delta stream + network partitions? I want to repro the 90s window.

olivia: Yes — add a `policy_skew` fault that delays deltas per-region and verify two things: (1) safety: no permanent misrouting, (2) performance: latency SLOs for critical routes under stale reads.

dominic: Action items:
- olivia: draft delta format + seq semantics (incl. tombstone/replace) — due EOD Tue
- ryan: prototype bloom-filter broadcaster + backoff math — due Thu
- maya: add sim scenarios to routing-sim and try to repro — due Wed

ryan: Also propose a rollout plan: canary policy-service -> 5% routers -> monitor penalty drift metric (`route_penalty_staleness_ms`) and error budget. If drift > 30s for critical tenants, pause.

maya: Ok thanks. This feels much safer than doing per-decision RPCs. I'll follow up with a short RFC doc and include a toy sequence diagram. :thumbsup:

dominic: Thanks all. If anyone wants to pair on the sim let me know.
